To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The key pathogenic mechanisms underlying AD are caused by a reduction of AHN due to a lack of environmental stimulation and by dysregulation of cortisol secretion, which is caused by avoidance of novelty.

“AD is a disease of the brain's memory center, which results from a failure of the brain's natural ability to rejuvenate its memory cells by adult hippocampal stem cell neurogenesis, which in turn results from a lack of physical and mental activity”.
the human brain is designed to memorize personal experience throughout life, and that AD is a consequence of a lifestyle that impairs AHN and causes dysregulation of HPA-axis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an integrative theory of the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease, which is based on a systems-biological model.

the question how lifestyle factors, genetic risk factors, environmental toxins and other risk factors for AD interact with each other in a causal chain and how they impair AHN and cause the development of AD.
the elucidation of the mechanisms by which lifestyle factors and environmental toxins affect the brain, particularly the adult hippocampus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AD is not a disease of the old but of the young, and that it is not a disease that is inevitable at old age but a preventable disease.

UTAD is the only currently available theory of AD that integrates all relevant key risk factors in a single coherent causal model, that is based on evolutionary and biological principles and that can be tested experimentally and clinically.
the human brain has a built-in self-optimization mechanism, which is based on AHN.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a causal treatment of Alzheimer's disease requires an individualized system biological approach, which targets the key risk factors of the Unified Theory of Alzheimer Disease (UTAD) in order to restore neuronal rejuvenation and the ability to memorize important personal experiences.
the UTAD is the most comprehensive theory of Alzheimer's disease that is currently known.
the UTAD is a unifying hypothesis that explains the pathogenetic mechanisms of AD and provides a rational basis for its causal treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the UTAD provides the basis for a system-biological understanding of AD that is based on a causal chain of pathogenic mechanisms and that can be used for the prevention of the disease as well as for a causal and curative treatment of AD patients.
the UTAD is a comprehensive and integrative theory that explains all major risk factors of AD and the pathogenic processes that lead to the clinical symptoms of the disease.
the AD process starts in early life and is driven by a combination of environmental and genetic risk-factors.
